title: Upgrade ah pin to 0.12.0 and retire the vitest-runner shim (GH#46 fixed upstream)
description:
espectacular v0.12.0 (released 2026-10-14) fixes GH#46 upstream: the batched runner now follows vitest 5's `JSON report written to <path>` notice — attribution reads the named report file (relative paths resolved against the invocation cwd, same parse cap), so stdout-only parsing no longer degrades every batch to per-binding fallback.

That makes tambor's workaround shim (tools/vitest-runner.sh, wired as `runners.vitest = ["sh", "tools/vitest-runner.sh"]` in .espectacular/config.toml) unnecessary. The shim exists purely to route json-mode invocations through `--outputFile=<mktemp>` + `cat` (tambor-8rq era, ah 0.11.0).

Scope:
1. Bump `.espectacular/config.toml` tool_version 0.11.0 -> 0.12.0 (and versions.ddl.toml pin if it carries ah).
2. Retire the shim: `runners.vitest` back to plain vitest; delete tools/vitest-runner.sh.
3. Re-measure the pre-push `espectacular-contracts` gate (per-gate timing is persisted in .gate-timing.log): expect the batched path (~28-30s measured with shim) to hold WITHOUT the shim, and zero `batch-fallback` findings in the ah check JSON envelope.
4. Result doubles as the evidence to close espectacular#40 (batching ticket).

Acceptance:
- Must: config pin at 0.12.0, shim file gone, one clean push with `ah check --run-tests` reporting zero batch-fallback findings.
- Meter: .gate-timing.log shows espectacular-contracts <= 60s with exit 0 on the upgrade commit's push.

Anti-goals: no vitest.config.ts changes beyond what shim removal requires (the per-reporter outputFile map from 8rq STAYS — it keeps the json reporter from clobbering the junit file testaruda ingests); no other gate changes.
notes: metadata.files: .espectacular/config.toml, tools/vitest-runner.sh (delete), versions.ddl.toml; base_commit bd7d944; links espectacular#40 (evidence to close), espectacular#46 (upstream fix); origin: user-approved ticket creation 2026-10-14 session

title: Adopt ah contract-execution batching (espectacular#40) once released: bump tool_version pin + versions.ddl.toml, expect push-time espectacular-contracts gate to drop from ~790s to ~60-90s
close_reason:
Adopted ah 0.11.0 (espectacular#40 batched contract execution). Pin bump: versions.ddl.toml + ci.yml install-action + .espectacular/config.toml tool_version -> 0.11.0 (160d8a3, pushed through all gates).

MEASURED: espectacular-contracts gate ~790-840s -> 29.98s (.gate-timing.log 2026-10-14T13:40:21Z). ~26x.

Required two tambor-side fixes the fallback masked:
1. vitest 5 ALWAYS routes --reporter=json to a file and prints a notice line on stdout; ah's batched parse of stdout failed -> 329/658 contracts degraded to per-binding fallback (12m8s, no win). Fixed with tools/vitest-runner.sh runner shim: json mode re-runs with --outputFile=mktemp and cats the clean JSON to stdout; per-binding exit-code runs pass through.
2. Global string outputFile in vitest.config.ts made CLI json overwrite target/test-results.xml (the junit file testaruda ingests) -> per-reporter object form { junit: ... }.
3. Batched attribution surfaced 4 example-todo contracts (p_enter, p_enter_unfocused, p_other_keys, p_new_todo_layout) as never having run: no vitest tests existed, and the pre-batching exit-code path passed zero-match invocations vacuously (vitest exits 0 on no matches). Wrote tests/example-todo-new-todo.test.ts (4 real tests, 333 total).

Residual observation for upstream: attribution matches binding patterns as substrings against fullName, so p_enter also matches p_enter_unfocused's tests (vacuous pass in the other direction). Filed upstream follow-up separately.

title: pre-push gate suite: measure per-gate cost, then parallelize or move calibration to CI
description:
Evidence (October pi sessions): tambor pushes p90 ~246s, worst observed 1123s; lefthook pre-push runs espectacular-contracts (ah check --run-tests), pretender-gate-full, testaruda-exec (incl. calibration) and one push reported (done in 603.40 seconds). 37 pushes this month = hours of gate-waiting inside agent turns.

Fix in two steps (measure first — 600s was worst-case, not median):
1. Instrument: per-gate duration logging in lefthook.yml (or a just recipe) -> capture distribution over ~10 pushes.
2. Act on data: enable job-level parallelism if serial, and/or move the testaruda calibration step to CI (it gates recall, not the push). Keep pretender gate local (fast, 0.35s).

TDD: red = test asserting per-gate timing output exists; green = instrument; refactor = restructure lefthook.yml per measurements.

comments.author: charly vibes
comments.text:
MEASURED (instrumentation landed in commit tools/gate-timing.sh + lefthook wiring; historical per-gate durations from lefthook summaries across 4+ pushes):
- espectacular-contracts (ah check --run-tests): 786-835s = ~93% of push cost. Root cause (verified in espectacular src/runner.rs::run_declared_tests): one runner process per contract — 658 sequential vitest spawns.
- testaruda-exec: 27-37s (calibration inside it measured <1s standalone)
- pretender-gate-full: 0.4-0.8s; scaffold-debt-report: 0.4-1.2s

DECISIONS ON DATA:
1. parallel: true — REJECTED: best case saves ~65s of ~850s (~7%) while stealing CPU from the dominant gate (both spawn vitest); contention risk exceeds savings.
2. Move calibration to CI — REJECTED: calibrate measured <1s; exec has no --skip-calibrate flag; upstream work for ~1s is not worth it.
3. REAL LEVER (filed): charly-vibes/espectacular#40 — batch contract execution per test file (junit-name attribution), expected 790s → ~60-90s. Tracked locally as tambor-8rq (pin bump on release).
Instrumentation stays: .gate-timing.log accumulates per-gate distribution on every push for verifying the batching win when it lands.

title: P2 bug CI: contract tests spawning tsc/bundler subprocesses exceed the 5s default vitest timeout on hosted runners (p_typescript failed in run 37831173691)

comments.author: charly vibes
comments.text: Root cause: vitest 5s default per-test timeout vs full-tsc subprocess tests (~3s warm local, >5s cold on hosted CI). Reproduced at --testTimeout=1500. Fix: per-test 30000ms on the four subprocess-heavy tests (p_strict, p_no_any, p_esm in typing-strict; p_typescript in tambor-core). pretender untouched — its scan is ~2s, far under the default. Local verification: vitest 325/325, ah check --run-tests 658 passed 0 findings, prettier clean, tsc --noEmit exit 0. Awaiting push authorization to confirm CI Green.

comments.author: charly vibes
comments.text: CI GREEN confirmed (run 37942868995, 34m23s, all 4 gates ✓). Full fix arc: (1) per-test 30s subprocess timeouts, 2584dbe; (2) testaruda adapters not in release tarballs — installed from git tag v0.5.1, d405a70; (3) bash -e made the exit-20 tolerance dead code (bare cmd aborts before code=$?), 6fa12c2; (4) exit 10 (uncalibrated) tolerated — CI store is ephemeral, calibration non-blocking (tambor-cpd). Known limitation documented: CI ingests 0 results until a testaruda release carries engine 4a51638 (collection_path ingest) + adapter 73ca44f (discovery ids).

title: testaruda calibration gate reports NOT CALIBRATED but does not block push; 7 test results unmatched to store items
description: Observed during tambor-8nt verification push (1806e66..fe05231, 2026-10-08): testaruda-exec output shows '7 run result(s) matched no known test item' (ids with HTML entities: tests/component-model.test.ts::p_forward: the rendered view's handlers..., p_fixed_position, p_wheel_child, p_cursor, p_first_match — escaping mismatch between adapter output and store items) and 'Predictive Ranking Calibration Gate: NOT CALIBRATED — recall 0.000 below threshold 0.800' yet the push proceeded (gate is non-blocking despite gate naming). With 0 actual failures recall is degenerate 0/0 — decide intended semantics: either fix id escaping so all results match, and/or make recall vacuously pass when actual failures == 0, and/or actually enforce blocking. Also decide whether 'NOT CALIBRATED' should ever be a silent pass.
acceptance_criteria: Must gate (quantified): testaruda exec locally reports 0 unmatched run results (entity-escaping fixed); the calibration gate either reports CALIBRATED (recall ≥ 0.8, or vacuous pass with the 0-failures case explicitly reasoned in this ticket) or blocks with a nonzero exit — never a silent NOT CALIBRATED pass. Meter: sh tools/gates/testaruda-exec.sh; regression anchor: npx vitest run tests/gate-timing.test.ts. Anti-goal: do not weaken or delete the calibration gate, do not game the store to force calibration.

comments.author: charly vibes
comments.text: Fresh evidence 2026-10-09: tambor CI now runs testaruda exec green but ingests 0 results — engine v0.5.1 passes only runner stdout to ingest while vitest junit goes to the collection_path file (upstream fix testaruda 4a51638 unreleased; release ticket filed in testaruda repo). Local 7-unmatched results = entity escaping (') mismatch, pre-73ca44f discovery ids excluded. Once testaruda v0.5.3 ships, bump tambor pins (testaruda 0.5.2→0.5.3 + adapters from tag) for real CI calibration.

comments.author: charly vibes
comments.text: Interim ruling recorded (was only implicit in code): the calibration gate is deliberately non-blocking — tools/gates/testaruda-exec.sh:14-21 tolerates exit 10 (store uncalibrated) and cites this ticket; tambor-8nt lineage. That decision stands unless reopened. Remaining open decisions narrowed to: (1) degenerate recall when actual failures == 0 (vacuous pass vs block), (2) whether NOT CALIBRATED may ever pass silently, (3) local id entity-escaping fix (' vs ') so all 7 results match store items. CI half (ingests 0 results, upstream engine bug) split to tambor-8q3 — real-CI verification waits on testaruda v0.5.3 there; the three local items above do not.

comments.author: charly vibes

comments.author: charly vibes
comments.text: Root cause of the 12 unmatched results located upstream in testaruda: adapter-typescript/src/main.rs::extract_xml_attr (~line 856) extracts junit <testcase> attribute values without unescaping XML entities. Vitest's junit reporter escapes ' -> ' and < -> < in name attributes, so run-result ids carry ' while store items (discovery via vitest JSON) carry raw '. Fix belongs upstream: unescape the five named entities in extract_xml_attr (or on extracted name/file values), replacing lt/gt/quot/apos before amp to avoid double-unescape of <. TDD shape: a junit fixture with name="it's <ok>" must ingest to id "it's <ok>" matching the discovery id. Context: tambor-8q3 pin bump (0.5.5) verified ingest > 0 locally (321 results); this escaping item is the remaining local-mismatch fix under this ticket.

comments.author: charly vibes
comments.text: Upstream follow-ups filed: testaruda-uwup (junit attribute XML-unescaping — root cause of the 12 local unmatched) and testaruda-7r9l (CI resolves only 60/333 vs local 321/333 with same tool and fresh store — CI-environmental matching bug). tambor-8q3 closed: CI now ingests >0 (60 results, run 38632309310 green). Once the upstream fixes ship and pins bump again, calibration gets real history and this ticket's three semantic decisions become decidable on real data.
